get_state.doc: Claim-reward gate for the desk. Returns { eligible, capped, step } for the CALLER, read from yp.reward_claim: eligible=1 when the row's status is 'clicked' or 'started' — being MAILED is an invitation, not an entitlement, so the user must have followed the campaign link — AND yp.reward_personal_eligible() says the caller can hold the prize. The prize is a personal yp.quota entitlement (5 years of unlimited storage), and entitlement resolution is tenant-first, so a user already covered by an organisation's row would have one written that is never read; they are turned away here rather than walked through the flow for nothing. This replaces the browser's localStorage latch, so the answer follows the user across devices and a re-send re-arms them. capped=1 means eligible but the campaign's limited slots (reward_conf.slots, default 100) are all taken: the desk shows the sold-out screen instead of the walkthrough, and step comes back empty because there is nothing to resume into.

track.doc: Record how far the caller got in the claim-reward flow (ui-team builtins/widget/reward-flow). One row per user in yp.reward_claim; status and step only ever advance, so a re-post can never undo a completion. Posting status='done' also REQUESTS one of the campaign's limited slots: yp.reward_claim_track awards it under a lock, or writes 'missed' when the cap has closed or the caller cannot hold the prize (reward_personal_eligible — an ineligible user must not consume a place). An awarded slot also GRANTS the prize in the same locked section: yp.reward_grant_storage writes the personal yp.quota entitlement for 5 years of unlimited storage, so a user can never take one of the campaign's places and receive nothing. `granted` carries the answer back — the only call whose result the widget must wait for.

step.description: step1 | step2 | step3 — the card step the user is on

granted.description: 1 when the caller holds a reward slot; 0 when a 'done' post was refused because the cap had closed
